Open discussion: Feminism in the first world

I come directly from tumblr on this. I am making the move from tumblr to originally reddit, until I realized exactly how bigoted reddit is. coming from a cesspool of "the dictionary definition-" and "not all feminists-," I want a breath of fresh air. Why do you believe feminism is needed in the first world? For the love of god don't site the wage gap or "manspreading." I want you to give me a reason to support your cause; that is a real inequality between genders in the first world.

I will preface this by saying that I have frequently acknowledged that women across all cultures face varying levels of oppressions in terms of severity. Obviously a woman in many Asian countries will face a far tougher road than one in most of Western Europe for example. This however does not negate the oppressions and victimizations that women even in the first world still face.

I will specifically talk about the U.S. Because that is what I am most familiar with. Regardless of the legal advancements that women have made over the last century we still face daily oppressions. We are cat called, talked down to, raped, murdered, dismissed, talked over, objectified, trapped into heterocaptivity, expected to perform parlor tricks for the entertainment of men, stared at and judged by physical attributes, the list goes on and on.

Contrary to popular belief I don't 'hate' or even blame men for their oppressive behavior, it is so ingrained in them that they are often not even aware of it themselves. Women have been under the control of the patriarchy for all of human history since the days of the rape caves. Because of this history, it is impossible for us to ever truly be on equal footing with men without dismantling the patriarchy.

This is why I have proposed many multigenerational plans, peacefully and following all legal channels based entirely on the voluntary actions of individuals I might add, to replace the current male dominated society with a female dominated society for a generation or two so that women can flourish for the first time in human history and have a chance of reaching true equality when men are reintroduced into the equation.

Whether you support our cause or not is entirely up to you. We don't seek advancement by force or browbeating, we presented our views and encourage an open exchange whether we agree or not. Many of us in the rational feminist movement even have differing opinions about specific issues. We face a great deal of vitriol and negativity and those who dismiss our movement but we have seen a surprising amount of growth even to us over the past year, and our platform was even reported on favorably in the Wall Street Journal not too long ago.

Riding a bike is not considered "working out" in the Netherlands, its a means of transportation. Its not subculture, it is culture. We ride these bikes while we wear our normal clothes (even from the gym while we just showered after working out).

Good bikes get stolen very often, especially in the innercities and Station areas (they say a junky can pick any lock in about 45 sec). Most people i know have 2 bikes, (1 Piece of Shit) for when you go to the pub and wich you can leave at the station for a while. And a decent solid practical bike with good gears, a rack on the back (for bags, taking someone with you on the back or whatever) and jacket protectors. You would leave this bike at a guarded bikestall (there are lots), use it on sunday or when you visit friends or relatives with a garage.

We do have a lot of bike parkings that look like the picture above (the Bike Boat, at Amsterdam Central) just walk past any highschool.

Why do bikes work in the Netherlands:

It's really really flat over here. No traffic jams (in many ways its much faster to cycle in the inner-cities then to use your car. We have an extensive bike infrastructure in the Netherlands, seperate lanes special "bike roads" etc. these are everywhere all across our country. Every dutchman riding in a car, knows how it feels when you ride a bike, so they take extra care of them. Most urban cities are old medievel infrastructure with newly build suburbs around them. You rarely have to ride further then 30 minutes to get to your destination. We get our drivers licenses at 18, Schoolbusses are none exsistent in the Netherlands, so you grow up with it. A bike is cheap. You can ride a bike intoxicated or drunk after a night out. We have a fierce Paid parking rage in the netherlands, parking on the streets in Amsterdam is around 4,50 euros an Hour. Plus you dont have to look for a parking spot. A lot of people ride their bike to the station when they take the train to work.

There are on average 2,6 bikes per Dutchman, we start riding them when we are very little. Most mom's bring their children to school on them ( a mom with a child in a seat on the handlebars and one on the backrack is not a rare sight). Our ministeries have actual "governement bikes" i could go on for a while :)
